transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (Arcadia), Priya Singh (Arcadia), Daniel Cortez (Arcadia)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/sales/arcadia-deck, https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/joint-pipeline-arcadia (joint pipeline sheet)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. want to run through the joint pipeline and make sure we're aligned on priorities and next steps for nova, meridian and clearwater. sound good?
[00:18] Liam: yes, thanks maya. quick note, we have a new contact at NovaBank, they're the head of payments product, should help push this along.
[00:32] Priya: timeline wise, nova is looking to decide by end of september, meridian is more of a q4 motion, clearwater is a longer pilot but high visibility.
[00:45] Maya: perfect, so nova is our primary win-bet. ethan, can you quick recap the technical ask?
[00:53] Ethan: yeah, from my call with daniel last week, nova wants private deployment into their vpc, plus fips-level key management, and low token latency for chat/agents. they also asked about offline/on-prem options for a small set of records.
[01:10] Daniel: correct, and one thing — our security team flagged SOC2 and ISO alignment, plus audit logs retention, basically standard enterprise checklist.
[01:24] Ethan: we can cover SOC2 and audit logs out of the box for hosted, but for private they want customer-managed k-m-s, which we support via KMS/HSM integrations. small caveat: the private package has different pricing and a slightly longer lead time for provisioning.
[01:44] Priya: when you say longer lead time, ballpark?
[01:47] Ethan: typically 3-5 weeks for enterprise private deployments, could be 2-4 weeks if infra ready and we have the contract signed. provisioning includes network setup, SSO, and optionally on-prem agent install.
[02:03] Liam: nova's security already has a list of must-haves, I'll push those to maya after this call.
[02:09] Maya: great, thanks. on the commercial side, the ask was for a pilot price for two weeks of eval at production-ish throughput, roughly 20k tokens/day. we proposed a discounted pilot plus commit option if they like the results.
[02:25] Priya: and what's the conversion motion after pilot? typical commit/discount bands?
[02:30] Maya: we usually propose a 3-month reserved capacity for dedicated or a private infra contract if they want isolation long-term; discount depends on commit size — we gave a preliminary 20-30% for first-year commit, can go higher for multi-year. details in the partner playbook link.
[02:46] Noah: also flag that arcadia often bundles a services credit for first implementation — that's a useful co-sell lever.
[02:54] Priya: yes, we typically do some services to help with integration which helps close faster.
[03:00] Ethan: technically, to hit their latency goals we can tune batching and use a quantized model variant; tradeoff is a small drop in some rare generation quality cases. worth aligning on SLOs up front.
[03:15] Daniel: can you quantify the latency we might see for a 256-token prompt on your dedicated infra?
[03:21] Ethan: on dedicated, p95 for 256 tokens is usually sub-200ms token-step depending on GPU. end-to-end response for a 256 token generation tends to fall in 400-700ms range. on private (customer VPC) numbers are similar but depends on network egress.
[03:40] Priya: competitors like Anthropic have different latency profiles; do you have a benchmark we can share?
[03:45] Maya: yes, i will share the perf benchmark spreadsheet — note that some labels are auto-generated and can be slightly noisy. link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/novabank-november.
[03:58] Liam: sounds good. switching to meridian, they're asking about multi-tenant isolation because they run a marketplace and don't want cross-customer leakage.
[04:08] Ethan: we can do per-tenant model pinning and per-tenant KV cache policies, also RBAC and per-route quotas in the console. small caveat: multi-tenant with strong isolation tends to prefer private/dedicated infra rather than shared hosted.
[04:25] Daniel: ok, that aligns with their ask. is there a standard SOW template for that?
[04:30] Maya: yes, ethan will draft a rough SOW and i will include pricing options.
[04:35] Ethan: i'll put together a checklist for the private deployment and a draft SOW, includes network diagram, expected SLAs, and fallback policies.
[04:45] Priya: for clearwater health, the compliance bar is highest — they asked about data residency in eu and additional audit support.
[04:54] Noah: arcadia's experience in healthcare will be useful here — priya can lead references.
[04:58] Priya: we can share two healthcare references later this week.
[05:03] Maya: brilliant. next, commercial alignment: do we have a preferred margin split for these co-sells?
[05:08] Noah: typical split is 70/30 in favor of arcadia for first year when they bring the customer, then re-evaluate on renewal. open to negotiation per deal size.
[05:20] Maya: okay we'll mirror that in the draft MSA.
[05:23] Liam: one ask from nova, they want a joint exec briefing with c-suite to get buy-in — can we prepare a 30-minute briefing?
[05:31] Maya: yes, we can do an exec briefing, maya will lead the deck and liam will coordinate timing.
[05:36] Priya: target timeline? they want it in the next two weeks.
[05:40] Maya: we can do it next monday or tuesday afternoons, i'll propose times after this call.
[05:45] Daniel: tech deep-dive for meridian — they'd like to see a demo of the private routing and model pinning.
[05:53] Ethan: i'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive next week; daniel and i will run through architecture, kv cache, and failure modes.
[06:02] Liam: quick question — what's the rollback story if a model update causes regressions?
[06:07] Ethan: we support model version pinning per-route and can do canary rollouts. console has automatic fallback policies; if a version regresses, you can revert to the prior version in minutes. we also surface quality regressions tied to eval prompt sets.
[06:22] Priya: good, that helps.
[06:25] Maya: pricing note — for pilots we can do a time-boxed discounted trial; if they convert to reserved we credit a portion of pilot fees. we'll put that in the playbook.
[06:36] Liam: on procurement, nova requires some legal standard clauses around liability and data handling. do you have a procurement pack?
[06:43] Maya: yes i'll share our procurement/legal pack and the standard msas. sometimes procurement needs a quicker redline turnaround, we can ask legal to prioritize.
[06:52] Priya: about discounts, if arcadia brings the lead and drives the first year commit, can arcadia get an increased referral fee?
[07:00] Noah: yes, we can consider an increased band for that scenario; we'll need to document in the partner agreement.
[07:06] Maya: shipping to next steps — i'll send the partner playbook, pricing matrix and the exec-briefing slides. ethan will prepare the private deployment checklist and SOW draft. liam will intro the nova exec sponsor. priya will share healthcare refs.
[07:18] Daniel: thanks. small nit — when you say "private" do you mean our private managed control plane or fully on-prem?
[07:25] Ethan: both options exist: Private (VPC) where we run the runtime in your cloud account or on-prem where you host machines. on-prem is more involved and often needs about 6-8 weeks. vpc/private is 3-5.
[07:38] Liam: that helps planning.
[07:41] Maya: any blockers from arcadia side to get these moving?
[07:44] Priya: none immediate, just need the docs and a clear timeline.
[07:48] Noah: also ask for a simple one-pager on the technical differences between hosted/dedicated/private, that helps our AE's pre-qual.
[07:57] Maya: we'll add that to the pack.
[08:00] Ethan: just to add, there's one tradeoff: heavy quantization + aggressive batching reduces cost but might affect certain rare output patterns — we should include a short eval set to monitor quality.
[08:13] Daniel: yeah, let's include that in the pilot.
[08:17] Maya: ok — jumping ahead, shall we review the three deals one-by-one? nova first.
[08:22] Liam: nova: pain is payments fraud prevention and chat ops for internal workflows. they want secure logs retention and real-time latency. our estimate for contract value is ~350k first year.
[08:35] Maya: good to know. our current ask is pilot for two weeks at a discounted rate; if they like results we push to a reserved private deployment at the 350k range.
[08:44] Priya: major obstacle is their procurement timeline. they want a clear contract and SSO + KMS in place.
[08:50] Maya: we'll prepare an accelerated procurement checklist.
[08:54] Ethan: reminder, for KMS we support AWS KMS and customer HSM — need to confirm vendor specifics.
[08:59] Liam: i'll check and follow up.
[09:02] Maya: meridian next — expected value ~120k first year, need marketplace isolation and per-tenant billing.
[09:11] Priya: they're also asking about model fine-tuning vs prompt engineering. would prefer to avoid fine-tuning initially.
[09:18] Ethan: fine-tuning adds ops overhead; recommend prompt engineering + few-shot techniques to start. we can propose a services block for later fine-tuning if needed.
[09:28] Maya: clearwater is a strategic healthcare reference; value uncertain but high strategic visibility. we should prioritize compliance and references.
[09:37] Noah: agree, that can open more leads in healthcare.
[09:40] Liam: anything else on mutual exclusivity or conflict with other partners?
[09:44] Noah: none known. arcadia is primary ref for healthcare in their region.
[09:48] Maya: ok, action items recap — see the pipeline sheet I'll update after call.
[09:55] Priya: we'll share the two healthcare references by friday.
[10:00] Maya: great — scheduling: ethan, can you do the meridian technical deep dive tuesday 16:00 UTC?
[10:06] Ethan: yes, works for me.
[10:09] Daniel: that's okay.
[10:11] Maya: lia, can you intro nova exec sponsor by monday?
[10:15] Liam: i'll get that done.
[10:18] Maya: any last questions?
[10:20] Priya: none from me.
[10:22] Noah: no.
[10:24] Maya: awesome, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the playbook and pricing matrix.
[10:28] Liam: thanks, talk soon.
[10:30] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic captions had occasional mislabels (e.g., "k-v cash" instead of "KV cache"), some product names auto-corrected incorrectly. This export preserves verbatim speech where possible.
